_meta.source_document: District Environmental Plan for Bengaluru Rural District, Karnataka State (2021)
_meta.extraction_method: PDF is a SCANNED / image-only document - pdftotext -layout returns empty and Tesseract OCR fails on the skewed CamScanner pages. Every numeric figure was therefore read visually: pages rendered with pdftoppm at 220-400 dpi, cropped with Pillow, and read as images directly.
_meta.page_label_convention: For this Bengaluru Rural document the printed footer label EQUALS the PDF page number (PDF page 38 carries footer '38|Page', PDF page 34 = '34|Page', etc.). No +N offset (unlike the Bengaluru Urban DEP). Citations give the printed label, which is also the PDF page.
_meta.scope_note: All three streams (hazardous, biomedical, C&D) are reported DISTRICT-wide in this DEP, not per-taluk. The only taluk-resolved facts are: (a) the single integrated TSDF is sited at Dabaspet, Nelamangala Taluk; (b) the C&D current-status table NAMES the five ULBs (City Municipal Council Hosakote, City Municipal Council Doddaballapura, City Municipal Council Nelamangala, Town Municipal Council Devanahalli, Town Municipal Council Vijayapura) but leaves every per-ULB C&D quantity cell BLANK. Doddaballapura, Nelamangala and Devanahalli (our taluks of interest) are all listed as ULB rows but carry no C&D tonnage.

hazardous_waste.facility_status: There is ONE integrated TSDF (Transport-Storage-Disposal Facility) inside the district, at Dabaspet, Nelamangala Taluk. No Sanitary Landfill Facility (SLF) and no standalone incinerators within the district. No contaminated or probable contaminated sites reported. 286 hazardous-waste-generating industries are recorded in the district.
hazardous_waste.page: DEP 2021, printed p.38 (PDF page 38); section 'V. Hazardous Waste Management - (a) Current status related to Hazardous Waste Management'. NOTE: the three sub-quantities (incinerable 4070.89 + landfillable 2190.73 + recyclable/utilizable 2187.84 = 8449.46) do NOT exactly equal the stated total of 8453.57 MT/Annum - a discrepancy of ~4.11 MT/Annum in the source. Reproduced verbatim.
hazardous_waste.notes: All five numeric figures (286 industries; 8453.57 total; 4070.89 incinerable; 2190.73 landfillable; 2187.84 recyclable) plus TSDF=01 at Dabaspet/Nelamangala, SLF=Nil, standalone incinerators=NIL, contaminated sites=NIL were each read directly from the page image at 220 and 400 dpi. The four MT/Annum values were re-confirmed in a tight side-by-side crop. The ~4 MT/Annum gap between the summed sub-quantities and the stated total is a source artefact, not an extraction error.

biomedical_waste.facility_status: BMW generated in the district is disposed to 03 Nos. CBMWTF (Common Bio-Medical Waste Treatment Facilities) located in / within 75 km of the district; all three CBMWTF have initiated a bar-coding system for tracking BMW lifting from HCFs. The district reports Covid-19 and non-Covid bio-medical waste being separately disposed through CBMWTF. Quantity generated equals quantity disposed (2292.96 kg/day). Action plan notes that where HCEs have no access to a CBMWTF, deep burial is practised in remote areas and HCEs are mandated to execute an MoU with a CBMWTF.
biomedical_waste.page: DEP 2021: HCF category breakdown table on printed p.34 (PDF page 34, '(iv) Bio-Medical Waste Management'); BMW generated/disposed quantity table (2292.96 kg/day each) on printed p.35 (PDF page 35); the '03 Nos. CBMWTF within 75 km' statement on printed p.36 (PDF page 36, bar-code/tracking action-plan row).
biomedical_waste.notes: BMW generated and disposed (both 2292.96 kg/day) read from the p.35 table image at 400 dpi (leading '22' sits at the cell's left edge but is legible). HCF category counts read from the p.34 table at 400 dpi. TWO category figures are the close-reading calls: 'Clinics, dispensaries' reads 396 at 400 dpi (a 220-dpi pass had suggested 398), and 'Research institutions' reads 01 at 400 dpi (220-dpi suggested 31). The 400-dpi reads (396, 01) are reported; both flagged for a human second look (p.34). No explicit grand-total HCF row is printed; 680 is our sum of the 9 rows. '03 Nos. CBMWTF' confirmed from the p.36 status text. Minor internal tension: p.36 says 03 CBMWTF serve the district, while the p.35 action plan also contemplates 'case of no access to CBWTF' - read as a generic action-plan template clause, not a contradiction of the 03 figure.

cnd_waste.facility_status: The district does NOT have access to a C&D waste recycling facility ('Does the District has access to C&D waste recycling facility? = No'). p.32: 'There is no C & D Recycling facility in the District.' p.32 also states 'There is no policy (Provisions) for usage or promotion of C&D waste in non-structural concrete, paving blocks, lower layers of road pavements, colony and rural roads.' ULBs do not have a sustained system of creating awareness on C&D Waste Management 2016 (IEC gap).
cnd_waste.page: DEP 2021, printed p.30 (PDF page 30); section '(iii) C & D Waste Management Rules - (a) Current status related to C & D Waste'. C&D gaps and action plan on printed p.31-p.32 (PDF pages 31-32).
cnd_waste.notes: The C&D current-status table on p.30 was read at 400 dpi. It contains the requirement row 'Total C&D waste generation in MT per day (As per data furnished by the ULB's)' and a nested ULB table with the 5 ULB names plus a 'Total' row, but the quantity column ('Quantity of C&D waste generation in TPD') is EMPTY for every ULB and for the Total - no TPD figures were furnished. This was confirmed by tightly cropping the cells immediately right of the ULB names (white / empty). The 'No' answer to 'access to C&D waste recycling facility' and the p.32 'no recycling facility / no usage policy' statements were image-verified. CONTRAST with Bengaluru Urban DEP (which had a fully populated per-ULB C&D table totalling 2507 TPD) - Bengaluru Rural's table is structurally identical but left unfilled.

extraction_caveats: This PDF is SCANNED / image-only (CamScanner). pdftotext returns empty and Tesseract OCR fails on the skewed pages, so EVERY figure here was read visually from page images rendered at 220-400 dpi, not from text extraction.

Hazardous waste: the three sub-quantities (incinerable 4070.89 + landfillable 2190.73 + recyclable/utilizable 2187.84 = 8449.46) do not sum exactly to the stated total 8453.57 MT/Annum - off by ~4.11 MT/Annum. Reproduced verbatim; a source rounding/transcription artefact. (p.38)

FLAG FOR HUMAN CHECK (p.34, biomedical HCF table): two category counts are close reading-calls. 'Clinics, dispensaries' read as 396 at 400 dpi (a lower-res 220-dpi pass had looked like 398). 'Research institutions' read as 01 at 400 dpi (220-dpi looked like 31). The 400-dpi values (396 and 01) are the ones reported. A human should re-verify these two cells on PDF p.34.

Biomedical: no explicit grand-total HCF count is printed in the source; the 680 total is OUR sum of the nine category rows (120+396+95+0+57+2+0+1+9). If a human re-reads 396->398 and/or 01->31, the total changes accordingly.

Biomedical: the inventory question header on p.35 mentions 'Existing No of HCFs in the District as per Annual report 2020-21' as a column, but that cell is not populated with a number in the p.35 quantity table - the HCF counts live in the separate p.34 category table (Annual Report 2021). Different annual-report vintages (2020-21 vs 2021 vs 2019 for the kg/day figure) appear in the document.

Biomedical: '03 Nos. CBMWTF within 75 km' (p.36) is the headline facility count; the p.35 action plan also references a generic 'case of no access to CBWTF' clause (deep burial / MoU). Read as boilerplate, not a contradiction.

C&D: this is the most important honest gap - the C&D current-status table on p.30 lists the 5 ULBs (incl. our taluks Doddaballapura, Nelamangala, Devanahalli) and a Total row, but EVERY C&D quantity (TPD) cell is BLANK. No district or per-taluk C&D tonnage exists in this document. The district explicitly has NO C&D recycling facility and NO C&D-reuse policy (p.30, p.32). Confirmed by image; contrast with Bengaluru Urban DEP whose identical table was fully populated (2507 TPD).

Granularity: all three streams are DISTRICT-wide. Only taluk-resolved fact is the single integrated TSDF at Dabaspet, Nelamangala Taluk. No hazardous or biomedical figures are broken out for Doddaballapura / Nelamangala / Devanahalli individually.
Page citations use the document's printed footer label ('N | Page'), which for this Bengaluru Rural document EQUALS the PDF page number (no offset).
